mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 700K units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 700K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 8%, indicating a strong labor market, and payroll employment (PAYEMS) shows a concurrent 3-month increase, the combined signal predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over 2 months, signaling supply chain disruptions, leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face increased costs and reduced output.
evidence_refs: fact:historical impact of supply disruptions on equity markets
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 55% of instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 2%, or Rank IC < 0.025 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: Positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days are predicted by the consistent growth in real disposable personal income (RSAFS), as it reflects sustained consumer spending power.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, indicating a tightening monetary cycle, and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) shows a concurrent increase above 3% over 6 months, the combined signal predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced borrowing and spending.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increase > 3% over 6 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 45% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 1% over 2 months, indicating labor market stress, leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending decrease.
evidence_refs: fact:historical impact of labor market shocks on equity markets
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 50% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 1%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: The consistent growth in GDP (GDPC1) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, reflecting the overall health and expansion of the economy.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.025 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
